title: Distinct Arithmetic Subsequences
statement:
You are given an integer array `a` of length `n` (0-indexed) and an integer `d`. Count the non-empty subsequences of `a` in which every pair of chosen positions `i < j` satisfies

`a[j] - a[i] = (j - i) * d`

Here `i` and `j` are the original positions in the array, not positions inside the subsequence. A subsequence with a single element always qualifies.

Two subsequences are different when their sets of chosen positions differ, even if they read the same values. Because the count can be huge, print it modulo `1000000007`.

For example, with `d = 2` the elements `a[1] = 5` and `a[3] = 9` can be chosen together, since `9 - 5 = (3 - 1) * 2`.
inputFormat:
The first line contains two integers `n` and `d`.
The second line contains `n` integers `a[0] ... a[n-1]`.
outputFormat: Print a single integer: the number of valid non-empty subsequences modulo `1000000007`.

examples.explanation: Compute a[i] - i*d for each position: 1, 1, 1, 0, 1. A set of positions is valid exactly when all of them share the same value. The value 1 occurs at 4 positions, giving 2^4 - 1 = 15 subsets, and the value 0 occurs once, giving 1 more. Total 16.
With d = 0 the chosen elements must be equal. Three positions hold 4, giving 2^3 - 1 = 7 subsets, and the single 7 gives 1 more. Total 8.
a[i] - i*d is 10, 10, 9, 10. Positions 0, 1 and 3 share the value 10 (7 subsets), position 2 stands alone (1 subset). Total 8.

hints: Take any two chosen positions i < j and rewrite a[j] - a[i] = (j - i) * d so that everything indexed by i is on one side and everything indexed by j is on the other.
The condition says a[i] - i*d equals a[j] - j*d. So a subset is valid exactly when every chosen position has the same transformed value.
Group positions by the transformed value. A group of size c contributes 2^c - 1 non-empty subsets; add them up modulo 10^9 + 7 (use fast modular exponentiation).
